# Static OG image for `/plan/share` Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship a branded static 1200×630 OG image for every URL under `/plan/share` so the share links generated by the Share My Plan feature unfurl as rich cards in iMessage, Slack, Twitter, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, and Discord.

**Architecture:** One new file at `app/plan/share/opengraph-image.tsx` using Next 16's file-based metadata convention — Next auto-wires it into `<meta property="og:image">` and `<meta name="twitter:image">` for the route. Mirrors the visual style and runtime decisions of the existing `app/opengraph-image.tsx` (homepage OG).

**Tech Stack:** Next 16 App Router, `next/og` `ImageResponse`, Node.js runtime (not Edge — Vercel Hobby 1MB Edge limit is the reason the homepage OG uses Node, per its inline comment).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-26-share-og-image-design.md`

---

| Path | Status | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `app/plan/share/opengraph-image.tsx` | Create | Renders the static 1200×630 PNG via `ImageResponse`. Exports `alt`, `size`, `contentType` constants per Next convention. |
| `__tests__/app/share-og.test.ts` | Create | Smoke test mirroring `__tests__/app/opengraph-image.test.ts`: imports the module, asserts the default export is a function and the exported constants are correct. |

Reference (do not modify): `app/opengraph-image.tsx` and `__tests__/app/opengraph-image.test.ts` — established pattern.

## Task 1: Static OG image + smoke test

**Files:**

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `__tests__/app/share-og.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'

describe('share-og opengraph-image', () => {
  it('exports a default function and the expected metadata constants', async () => {
    const mod = await import('../../app/plan/share/opengraph-image')
    expect(typeof mod.default).toBe('function')
    expect(mod.size).toEqual({ width: 1200, height: 630 })
    expect(mod.contentType).toBe('image/png')
    expect(typeof mod.alt).toBe('string')
    expect(mod.alt.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
    expect(mod.alt).toMatch(/plan|NYTW/i)
  })
})
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test, verify it fails**

Run: `npx vitest run __tests__/app/share-og.test.ts`
Expected: FAIL — `Cannot find module '../../app/plan/share/opengraph-image'`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `app/plan/share/opengraph-image.tsx`**

```tsx
import { ImageResponse } from 'next/og'

// Note: runtime='edge' caused 1.06 MB function (over Vercel Hobby's 1 MB limit).
// Default Node.js runtime has a much higher limit and OG images are cached by
// social platforms anyway, so cold-start difference is irrelevant.
export const alt = `A friend shared their NYTW plan with you — open to see what they picked for Tech Week NYC 2026`
export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }
export const contentType = 'image/png'

export default async function Image() {
  return new ImageResponse(
    (
      <div
        style={{
          width: '100%',
          height: '100%',
          display: 'flex',
          flexDirection: 'column',
          justifyContent: 'space-between',
          background: '#000000',
          padding: '72px',
          fontFamily: 'ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace',
        }}
      >
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8 }}>
          <div
            style={{
              color: '#FF5B25',
              fontSize: 28,
              letterSpacing: 4,
              textTransform: 'uppercase',
            }}
          >
            Tech Week NYC · June 1–7, 2026
          </div>
        </div>

        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 24 }}>
          <div
            style={{
              display: 'flex',
              flexDirection: 'column',
              color: '#F5F5F5',
              fontSize: 80,
              fontWeight: 800,
              lineHeight: 1,
            }}
          >
            <span>Someone shared their</span>
            <span>NYTW plan with you.</span>
          </div>
          <div
            style={{
              display: 'flex',
              color: '#9B9B9B',
              fontSize: 36,
              lineHeight: 1.2,
            }}
          >
            <span>Open to see what they picked.</span>
          </div>
        </div>

        <div
          style={{
            display: 'flex',
            justifyContent: 'flex-end',
            color: '#9B9B9B',
            fontSize: 24,
          }}
        >
          nytw.dev/plan
        </div>
      </div>
    ),
    { ...size }
  )
}
```

```bash

```
Expected output: lines containing `property="og:image"` and `name="twitter:image"` with URLs pointing to `/plan/share/opengraph-image…`.

b. Fetch the image directly to confirm it renders:
```bash
curl -sI https://nytw.dev/plan/share/opengraph-image
```
Expected: `HTTP/2 200` and `content-type: image/png`.

c. Sanity-check the visual via Twitter Card Validator (paste a real share URL — `https://nytw.dev/plan/share#someTestPayload`) at https://cards-dev.twitter.com/validator. Confirm the headline reads "Someone shared their NYTW plan with you."

If any of these fail, stop and investigate before declaring done.

## Self-review

**Spec coverage:**
- Static branded OG, no personalization → Step 3 ships exactly one image, no input variation.
- 1200×630 PNG, Node.js runtime → `size` constant and inline runtime comment match spec.
- Visual: black bg, `#FF5B25` eyebrow, `#F5F5F5` headline, `#9B9B9B` subhead + footer, 72px padding, mono font → all present in Step 3 JSX.
- Copy: "TECH WEEK NYC · JUNE 1–7, 2026" / "Someone shared their NYTW plan with you." / "Open to see what they picked." / "nytw.dev/plan" → all present, user-approved.
- File-based Next 16 convention auto-wires `og:image` + `twitter:image` → no `metadata` edits to `page.tsx` required; Step 10a verifies the tags are emitted after deploy.
- Test asserts default export type + `size` + `contentType` + non-empty `alt` mentioning plan or NYTW → Step 1 matches.

**Placeholders:** none — every step has either complete code, an exact command, or a concrete check with expected output.

**Type consistency:** `alt` / `size` / `contentType` / `default` export names match the spec, match the test assertions in Step 1, and match the existing homepage OG file convention. The test in Step 1 references `mod.alt`, `mod.size`, `mod.contentType`, and `mod.default` — all of which the Step 3 implementation provides.
